newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch building development project in German hands.
newsitem.headline: Dutch building development project in German hands.

text.p: Commerz Grundbesitz Investment GmbH (CGI) of Germany, which operates an open-end investment fund, is to take over the main part of a building project in the Dutch town of Amstelveen, the Amstelveen Ontwikkelingsmaatchappij said on Wednesday.

The project involves the renovation and expansion of some 40,000 square metres of shopping space, 16,000 of office space, 6,000 of cultural facilities, 180 apartments and 2,200 parking spaces, and should be concluded around the year 2000.
The transaction is worth over 600 million guilders, the statement said.

CGI -- which is 75 percent owned by Commerzbank and 25 percent held by DBV/Winterthur and has total assets worth 6.8 billion German marks -- operates the Haus Invest fund, in which some 175,000 retail customers invest.

The selling party, Stadshart Amstelveen Ontwikkelingsmaatschappij is a cooperation between the municipality of Amstelveen, the MAB/Bouwfonds Financiering Vastgoed and Dutch building company Ballast Nedam IGB. Amstelveen lies just south of Amsterdam.
